title: Unique tensor-model transition for arbitrary strict point systems
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with geometric algebraic closure k, a prime l, and a finite extension E of Q_l, with independent site and coefficient universes [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let g: Spec(k) -> Spec(k) be any scheme automorphism. Write B_n for the constant coefficient sheaf R/(varpi^(n+1)), S for the category of actual strict B_n-module systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], P_n for finite module pullback along g [def-pur-integral-finite-pullback], and Res_n for restriction through the completed coefficient projection [def-sf-scalar-reduction-categories-restriction]. Let T_n=Res_n P_n ev_n. For U a pro-etale object and x in M_(n)(gU), let j_(n,M,U)(x) be the pullback adjunction-unit generator at gU restricted along the canonical comma arrow, namely the sheafified tensor-unit insertion [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. There exists a unique natural transformation tau:T_(n+1) -> T_n such that, for every strict system M, every U, every a in B_(n+1)(U) and x in M_(n+1)(gU), tau_(M,U)(a*j_(n+1,M,U)(x))=rho_n(U)(a)*j_(n,M,U)(v_n(gU)(x)). Here v_n is the original horizontal transition of M and rho_n is coefficient reduction. No condition on l relative to the characteristic, no cartesianness, boundedness, constructibility, or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed; g may be the identity and transitions may be arbitrary, including zero.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-point-system-finite-tensor-comparison to identify finite sectionwise inverse image with the actual tensor pullback by the normalized tensor-unit isomorphism. Compose it with the identity-on-sections finite evaluation and completed scalar-restriction comparisons of lem-trf-point-system-ordinary-evaluation-comparisons. This gives a natural isomorphism from each completed-restricted reindexed system level to its finite tensor-pullback level, with the specified insertion on every original section.

proof.text: The concrete completed scalar restriction of def-coef-ringed-sequence-site retains every horizontal restriction. Apply it to the actual reindexed system of lem-trf-point-restriction-system-chain-map and conjugate its adjacent transition by the two level comparison isomorphisms. This is a natural completed-linear sheaf morphism. Cancelling the inverse comparison proves its value on an insertion is the insertion of the original transition.

proof.text: The coefficient naturality square in lem-trf-point-restriction-system-chain-map, inverted at both finite levels, says rho(gU)(c_(n+1)^(-1)(a))=c_n^(-1)(rho(U)(a)). The scalar normalization of lem-trf-point-system-tensor-insertion-scalars converts a times insertion(x) into insertion(c_(n+1)^(-1)(a)x). The original horizontal restriction is quotient-linear, so the preceding identity and the unit-insertion formula give the required generator formula, with every original transition retained. For uniqueness, precompose two candidate natural transformations by the source comparison isomorphism. Their section maps agree by the generator formula at a=1. Sheaf and natural-transformation extensionality give equality; cancel the isomorphism.

mathlib_searches.query: Conjugating the maps in a diagram by natural isomorphisms gives unique transition maps that agree on all sections
mathlib_searches.results: General diagram isomorphisms, including HasColimit.isoOfNatIso, LimitPresentation.changeDiag and GlueData.diagramIso; none specifies strict varying-coefficient tensor transitions.

CategoryTheory.NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.NatIso proves invertibility from component invertibility. It supplies one elementary step, not the normalized coefficient transition theorem.
SheafOfModules.pushforwardComp and pushforwardCongr have identity-on-sections component lemmas. They construct evaluation comparisons but do not state the required coefficient-compatible transition.

theorem tensor_transition_existsUnique (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! τ :
      (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) (n + 1) ⋙
        integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g (n + 1) ⋙
          scalarReductionRestriction l E (Spec (.of D.k)) (n + 1)) ⟶
      (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n ⋙
        integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g n ⋙
          scalarReductionRestriction l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n),
      ∀ (M : coefficientSequenceModules l E (Spec (.of D.k)))
        (U : (Spec (.of D.k)).ProEt)
        (a : (integralCoefficientSheaf l E (Spec (.of D.k)) (n + 1)).obj.obj (op U))
        (x : ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) (n + 1)).obj M).val.obj
          (op ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U))),
        (τ.app M).val.app (op U)
          (a • (((integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g (n + 1)).obj
            ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) (n + 1)).obj M)).val.map
              (proEtaleIsoCommaArrow g U).op
                (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E g (n + 1)
                  ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) (n + 1)).obj M)
                  ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U) x))) =
          (integralCoefficientSheafTransition l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).hom.app (op U) a •
            (((integralOperationsLevelPullback.{t, u} l E g n).obj
              ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).obj M)).val.map
                (proEtaleIsoCommaArrow g U).op
                  (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E g n
                    ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n).obj M)
                    ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U)
                    (M.val.presheaf.map
                      (Prod.mkHom (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n))
                        (𝟙 ((proEtaleIsoPostcompose g).obj U))).op x)))
